summary.oneLiner: Chatha Foods achieved 18% YoY revenue growth in FY25 driven by QSR customer acquisition and artisan product expansion, but margins were pressured by labor-intensive production; the company now has three clear growth levers — automation reducing labor costs, a new 16K MT vegetarian facility launching in Sept 2025, and a JV for exports — all poised to lift margins and revenue in FY26 and beyond.

hero.industry: QSR Frozen Food & Food Service Ingredients

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Chicken unit: 96% of revenue, 80% capacity utilization, 60-80% share with Domino's/Subway; Veg unit (new): 16,000 MT capacity, 60% export focus, products include tortillas, parathas, samosas, retorted rice; JV: 180-190cr revenue target, 100% export-bound via Allana

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: KFC marination trial commencing Aug 2025 (60-65 MT/month initially); no other order book disclosed

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: 20% YoY for FY26 (chicken unit); margin: Improving due to automation and veg unit ramp-up; order inflow: KFC trial starting Aug 2025; capex/commissioning: Veg unit (INR16K MT) to be fully operational by Sept 2025; JV unit by Nov 2025

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Export market entry via Allana JV (85 countries); vegetarian segment margin uplift; potential capacity expansion for KFC if marination trial succeeds; product IP licensing to other QSRs

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin down to 27% in FY25 due to 30% shift to labor-intensive artisan products (+INR60-70L labor cost); automation (imported cutting line) now deployed; veg unit expected to have higher margins than chicken; export margins projected to be significantly higher than domestic

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds: INR31cr utilized; remaining proceeds in bank deposits; no dividend policy disclosed; focus on capex for veg/JV units; no buybacks or M&A mentioned

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, proactive, and transparent; acknowledged margin pressures and credit risks but emphasized automation and new capacity as solutions; strong emphasis on export potential and customer collaboration; no defensiveness on past margin erosion

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material volatility (vegetables); credit risk from extended receivables (60 days vs target 50-55 days); export market entry execution risk; competition from Darshan Foods, Venky's, Sneha Farms; plant commissioning delays (already experienced with veg unit due to layout changes)

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 16K MT veg capacity is not fungible with chicken — it's a dedicated, high-throughput line for breads and frozen products; the 'artisan' product shift was a strategic pivot, not a cost mistake; the small existing veg unit (4,500 sq ft) is being decommissioned and merged into chicken plant — a hidden capacity gain
